title.rendered: Declaring Over Your Work and Labour: The Beauty of the Lord Upon Us | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 11

excerpt.rendered: Deuteronomy 28 commands the blessing on the work of your hands, and Psalm 90 asks for the beauty of the Lord upon our labour. Day 11 teaches believers how to declare over work.

content.rendered:
Moses asked for the beauty of the Lord upon the work of our hands. Twice. He understood what many believers forget, your labour is a place of declaration.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, October 28, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 11

Today’s Scripture

“Now it shall come to pass, if you diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God, to observe carefully all His commandments… all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you… Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the country… Blessed shall be the fruit of your body, the produce of your ground and the increase of your herds… The Lord will command the blessing on you in your storehouses and in all to which you set your hand.”
Deuteronomy 28:1-8 (NKJV, abridged)

“And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.”
Psalm 90:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Deuteronomy 28 is the Scripture Perry’s father would call “the blessing manifesto.” The NKJV stacks blessing upon blessing, and the AMPC adds the stunning detail that these blessings “shall come upon you and overtake you.” The TPT rendering of Psalm 90:17 is tender: “Let the sweet beauty of our Lord our God rest upon us and give us favour. Confirm, O God, this work that we’ve done; yes, establish the work of our hands.” Scripture speaks of your work not as a necessary evil but as a sanctuary, a place where the beauty of the Lord rests and the blessing of the Lord is commanded.

In Lagos, a developer deploys code before the dawn. In London, a nurse clocks in for a long shift. In Manila, a teacher gathers chalk and lesson plans. In Nairobi, a trader opens the shop grille. In São Paulo, an engineer boots a laptop and prays. In every one of those cities, there is a believer about to spend eight to twelve hours in a workplace. If we do not declare over our work, we hand our hours over to the mood of the office. Declaration keeps our labour under Christ’s Lordship.

Jesus Himself worked. For most of His life He was known as “the carpenter’s son” (Matthew 13:55). Heaven’s King knew what sawdust tasted like. He taught that even the smallest task, a cup of cold water, could be a kingdom act (Matthew 10:42). Paul wrote, “Whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men” (Colossians 3:23). Work is worship when it is offered under declaration.

So declare it on the commute. Declare it in the parking lot. Declare it before the inbox opens. Pastors, declare it over the pulpit on Sunday morning. Business owners, declare it over the quarterly plan. Students, declare it over the dissertation. Mothers, declare it over the laundry pile and the Sunday roast. The beauty of the Lord rests on the labour of a declaring believer.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. God commands blessing on “all to which you set your hand.” Your labour is not neutral; it is a field where God wants to plant harvest.

Personalise. Name your actual workplace. Your industry. Your clients. Your projects. Your pay. Faith is specific. Vague prayers over work bear vague fruit.

Proclaim. Speak Psalm 90:17 before you begin (“Establish the work of my hands, O Lord”), and Deuteronomy 28 as you walk through your day.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that the Lord commands the blessing on everything to which I set my hand. The beauty of the Lord my God rests upon me, and He establishes the work of my hands; yes, He establishes the work of my hands. I am blessed in the city and blessed in the country, blessed in my coming in and blessed in my going out, blessed in my storehouses, blessed in my offices, blessed in my inbox. I work heartily, as to the Lord. I am faithful in the little. Promotion comes not from the east or the west, but from God. Doors no man can shut swing open at the voice of my King. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
